HextaUI and shadcn/ui

HextaUI is not a replacement for shadcn/ui. It is a registry you add to a shadcn/ui project, with the same CLI, the same component names and the same theme tokens. This page explains what it adds and when you don’t need it.
HextaUI is not a replacement for shadcn/ui. It uses the same CLI, names and theme tokens, and adds finished states, motion, extra components and AI blocks.
HextaUI vs shadcn/ui: what HextaUI adds on top
Motion you can interrupt. Animations share one set of easing curves and durations, can be reversed halfway and turn into a fade when reduced motion is on.
Styling uses the same theme tokens, such as `--background`, `--primary` and `--radius`, with Tailwind CSS v4.

Touch, right-to-left and high contrast. Tap targets grow on touch screens, text inputs stay at 16px so iOS doesn’t zoom, layouts mirror for right-to-left languages and focus rings stay visible in Windows high contrast mode.

Use shadcn/ui when you want a clean starting point and plan to write the loading, error and empty states yourself. Add HextaUI when you want those states, the motion and the accessibility details already done, or when you need a component shadcn/ui doesn’t ship. You can mix both in one project, one component at a time.

When shadcn/ui alone is the better choice
You depend on the shadcn/ui blocks, charts and themes, or on the community Vue and Svelte ports. HextaUI is React only.
You install with the shadcn CLI, and the source is copied into your project. Nothing is locked inside a package.
You need the largest community and the most third-party examples. shadcn/ui has far more of both.
You want Radix primitives. HextaUI components are built on Base UI only.
You want the smallest possible component and would rather add states and motion yourself. HextaUI components carry more code because they handle more cases.
